Class LessonsLearned

java.lang.Object
entityClasses.LessonsLearned
public class LessonsLearned extends Object

Title: LessonsLearned Class

Description: This LessonsLearned class represents a single lesson learned entity in the system, together with the persistent Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations and the input validation that every one of the Contributor user stories relies on. It is the TP2 counterpart of the supplied User entity class and is written in the same plain attributes with getters and setters style, so that the two sit comfortably in the same package.

A lesson models the kind of item the team saw on the Ed Discussion board: a question or an observation, the reply that resolved it, and the person who contributed it. To that HW2 shape TP2 adds keywords for searching, the dates the lesson was created and last changed, and three attributes that the TP3 staff epics need (a review status, a reviewer comment, and a helpful count). The TP3 attributes are stored now, rather than added in TP3, because adding columns to a table that already holds data is the riskiest kind of change this project makes; see the TP1 note in Database.createTables. Contributors cannot change those three attributes: there are no setters for them, and LessonsLearnedDatabase.updateLesson leaves their columns out of its SET clause.

Two TP3 needs are deliberately not met by attributes here. Recording who found a lesson helpful, so one reader cannot count twice, needs a separate table keyed by lesson and user; the helpfulCount attribute is the total that table will maintain. Likewise, comments from several readers belong in their own table keyed by lesson identifier.

How the class supports each Contributor user story (the stories, CS-1 to CS-12, are listed in "Requirements to Tests Map.pdf" in the TP2 folder):

  • CS-1 Create: create(LessonsLearnedDatabase)
  • CS-2, CS-3 Read: read(LessonsLearnedDatabase, int) and the getters
  • CS-4 Search: matches(String), used by LessonsLearnedList.searchByText
  • CS-6, CS-9 Ownership: isOwnedBy(String)
  • CS-7 Update: update(LessonsLearnedDatabase)
  • CS-8 Delete: delete(LessonsLearnedDatabase)
  • CS-10, CS-11 Validation: validate(), which create and update both call
  • CS-12 Persistence: every operation goes through LessonsLearnedDatabase

The class has no JavaFX reference, so the testing automation can create, store, read, change, and delete lessons without opening a window.

    • REVIEW_NOT_REVIEWED

    • DATE_FORMAT

      public static final DateTimeFormatter DATE_FORMAT
      The format used for the two date attributes, chosen so that text order is date order.

    • id

      private int id
      Source: CS-3, CS-7, CS-8. Assigned by the database, -1 until the lesson is stored. An identifier is used to name a lesson, rather than its title, because the title can change.

    • title

      private String title
      Source: CS-1, CS-2. The one line shown in the list. Required, at most 80 characters.

    • category

      private String category
      Source: CS-1, CS-5. A short label used to group lessons and to filter by category. Required, at most 30 characters.

    • description

      private String description
      Source: CS-1, CS-3. The question or observation the lesson is about. Required, because a lesson with only a title records that something happened but not what.

    • resolution

      private String resolution
      Source: CS-1, CS-7. The reply that resolved the question. Optional, because a lesson can be recorded the moment a problem is noticed and resolved later by an update.

    • keywords

      private String keywords
      Source: CS-4. A comma separated list of words that the search also looks at, so a lesson can be found by a word that does not appear in its title or description. Optional.

    • contributor

      private String contributor
      Source: CS-1, CS-6, CS-9. The username of the account that created the lesson. It is set from the logged in user by the screens, never typed, so it cannot be used to impersonate someone, and it is what the ownership rule compares against.

    • dateCreated

      private String dateCreated
      Source: CS-2, CS-3. When the lesson was created, so the list can show the newest first and a reader can judge how current it is. Set once by create(LessonsLearnedDatabase).

    • dateUpdated

      private String dateUpdated
      Source: CS-3, CS-7. When the lesson was last changed, so a reader can see an edited lesson has been edited. Set by create(LessonsLearnedDatabase) and by every update(LessonsLearnedDatabase).

    • reviewStatus

      private String reviewStatus
      Source: TP3 staff epic (reviewing lessons). The outcome of a staff review. Stored now so the schema does not need to change in TP3; contributors can see it but not change it.

    • reviewerComment

      private String reviewerComment
      Source: TP3 staff epic (reviewing lessons). The reviewer's comment to the contributor.

    • helpfulCount

      private int helpfulCount
      Source: TP3 epic (marking a lesson as helpful, from the HW2 LessonShare evaluation). How many readers found the lesson helpful. Starts at zero.

      public LessonsLearned(String title, String category, String description, String resolution, String keywords, String contributor)

      Method: LessonsLearned(String title, String category, String description, String resolution, String keywords, String contributor)

      Description: The constructor used when a contributor is creating a brand new lesson. No identifier and no dates are supplied, because create(LessonsLearnedDatabase) sets them when the lesson is stored.

      category - the area the lesson belongs to
      description - the question or observation itself

      keywords - the comma separated keywords, which may be empty
      contributor - the username of the person contributing the lesson

  • Method Details

    • create

      public LessonInputPolicy.Problem create(LessonsLearnedDatabase db)

      Method: Problem create(LessonsLearnedDatabase db)

      Description: Stores this lesson as a new row (CS-1). The lesson is validated first and nothing is written if any field is refused, so an invalid lesson can never reach the database (CS-10, CS-11). Both dates are set to now, and on success the identifier the database assigned is recorded in this object so that it can be updated or deleted straight away.

      Parameters:
      db - the open lessons database
      Returns:
      null when the lesson was stored, otherwise the problem that stopped it

    • read

      public static LessonsLearned read(LessonsLearnedDatabase db, int id)

      Method: static LessonsLearned read(LessonsLearnedDatabase db, int id)

      Description: Reads the stored lesson with the given identifier (CS-3). It is static because there is no lesson object to call it on until the row has been read.

      Parameters:
      db - the open lessons database
      id - the identifier to read
      Returns:
      the stored lesson, or null when no lesson has that identifier

    • update

      public LessonInputPolicy.Problem update(LessonsLearnedDatabase db)

      Method: Problem update(LessonsLearnedDatabase db)

      Description: Writes the current values of this lesson back to its row (CS-7). The same validate method used by create is called first, so an edit cannot put a lesson into a state that creation would have refused. The update date is set to now; the creation date and the contributor are never changed by an update.

      The ownership rule (CS-9) is enforced by the lesson editor before this is called, rather than here, because this method does not know who is logged in.

      Parameters:
      db - the open lessons database
      Returns:
      null when the row was updated, otherwise the problem that stopped it

    • delete

      public boolean delete(LessonsLearnedDatabase db)

      Method: boolean delete(LessonsLearnedDatabase db)

      Description: Removes this lesson's row (CS-8). Asking the contributor to confirm is the screen's job, because the removal cannot be undone and only the screen can ask. On success the identifier goes back to -1, so this object no longer claims to be stored.

      Parameters:
      db - the open lessons database
      Returns:
      true when a row was removed, false when no lesson had this identifier

    • validate

      public LessonInputPolicy.Problem validate()

      Method: Problem validate()

      Description: Applies every input rule to this lesson's current values by calling LessonInputPolicy.validateLesson (CS-10, CS-11). The rules themselves live in the validation package, next to the TP1 rules, so that the editor screen can check a single field without building a lesson, and so the tests can exercise each rule on its own.

      Returns:
      null when every field is acceptable, otherwise the first problem found

    • isOwnedBy

      public boolean isOwnedBy(String userName)

      Method: boolean isOwnedBy(String userName)

      Description: Reports whether the given account contributed this lesson (CS-6, CS-9). The comparison is exact, because usernames are unique and case is part of a username in the supplied database.

      Parameters:
      userName - the username of the logged in account
      Returns:
      true when that account is this lesson's contributor

    • matches

      public boolean matches(String term)

      Method: boolean matches(String term)

      Description: Reports whether the term appears in the title, the description, or the keywords, ignoring case (CS-4). The keywords are included in TP2 so a contributor can make a lesson findable by a word that does not appear in its text. An empty term matches nothing, because an empty search is not a request to see everything.

      Parameters:
      term - the search term
      Returns:
      true when the lesson contains the term

      a single formatted line describing this lesson
